findings.matters: Best Value Inspection findings and Ministerial Envoy appointment signal governance and financial control failures that directly affect council stability and creditworthiness.
findings.figures: Inspection announced 12 November 2024; intervention agreed January 2025
findings.quote: The outcome of the Best Value Inspection was announced on 12 November 2024 with several recommendations and the agreement to appoint Ministerial Envoys to support the Council.

findings.headline: Council committed to external review of Investigations function with March 2026 deadline
findings.detail: The council has accepted the recommendation and implemented a 'Value for Money Response Mobilisation Plan' to address it. A new Team Leader was appointed in September 2025, and the council committed to an independent external review of the entire Investigations function to be completed by 31 March 2026, with concurrent policy reviews and documentation improvements.
findings.matters: The tight timeline and external review commitment signal the council recognises this as urgent, but also that remediation will be ongoing through Q1 2026—lenders need to track whether improvements are delivered on schedule
findings.figures: Team Leader appointed September 2025; external review completion date 31 March 2026
findings.quote: The council has committed to commissioning an external review of the Investigations function to be completed by 31 st March 2026. This will provide independent assurance and support the development of a more consistent and transparent framework.

findings.headline: External auditor identified significant governance weaknesses in internal investigations process
findings.detail: EY found that Tower Hamlets' internal investigations function lacks clarity, proportionality, and transparency. The auditor's recommendation requires the council to review team structure and capacity, strengthen investigation policies and procedures, ensure transparent decision-making with documented rationale, and clarify oversight and reporting arrangements.
findings.matters: Internal investigation processes are a critical governance control; identified weaknesses suggest gaps in the council's ability to conduct fair, consistent investigations into conduct matters—a fundamental control for public accountability
findings.figures: New Team Leader appointed September 2025; external review deadline 31 March 2026
findings.quote: The Internal Investigations function must operate with clarity, proportionality, and transparency. Aspects of the current approach require refinement to ensure consistency in standards, clearer accountability, and improved integration with the wider assurance framework.

findings.headline: Systematic quality failures in financial statements: missing notes, calculation errors, and unresolved prior-year valuation disputes
findings.detail: Draft financial statements contained internal inconsistencies, arithmetic errors, and omitted required disclosures (exit packages note missing). Management was unable to provide timely quality working papers for debtors, creditors, payroll and HRA. Property valuation issues raised in 2023/24 audit remain unresolved; management has engaged new valuation specialist for 2025/26.
findings.matters: Quality failures in accounts preparation indicate insufficient finance team resources or capability. Unresolved property valuation disputes spanning multiple years raise concerns about either the robustness of the valuation process or quality of evidence management can produce.
findings.figures: Quality of working papers rated 'Ineffective' for key accounting estimates; valuation issues unresolved across 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.quote: There were several internal inconsistencies, typographical and arithmetic errors in the draft financial statements, including the omission of the exit packages note.

findings.headline: Ten significant weaknesses in value for money arrangements identified; fraud controls assessed as not effective
findings.detail: Initial risk assessment identified seven potential weaknesses; auditors found five actual weaknesses plus an additional five during further procedures, totalling ten significant weaknesses in value for money. Auditors assessed management's fraud controls as not effective and identified five non-compliance with laws and regulations matters, primarily relating to procurement.
findings.matters: Multiple value for money weaknesses indicate systematic governance and control failures. Ineffective fraud controls and unresolved legal non-compliance (particularly in procurement) represent potential financial and reputational exposure for the council and credit risk for lenders.
findings.figures: 10 significant weaknesses in value for money arrangements; 5 statutory recommendations; 5 non-compliance with laws and regulations matters
findings.quote: we are reporting ten significant weaknesses in the Council's value for money arrangements and an additional statutory recommendation in relation to our 2024/25 audit.

findings.headline: £2.442m uncorrected audit misstatements reduce reserves, with net impact of £4.514m across audit cycles
findings.detail: Auditors identified uncorrected misstatements in 2024/25 totalling £2.442 million that increase expenditure and reduce reserves. When combined with prior year turnaround misstatements, the cumulative impact reduces expenditure by £4.514 million.
findings.matters: Uncorrected misstatements directly reduce reported reserves, the council's financial cushion. A £2.4m reduction in reserves in a single year affects the council's financial flexibility and its ability to meet future pressures without borrowing.
findings.figures: Uncorrected misstatements 2024/25: £2.442m; cumulative impact with turnarounds: £4.514m net reduction
findings.quote: Uncorrected misstatements identified in the 2024/25 audit increase expenditure and reduce reserves by £2.442 million.

findings.headline: Management has imposed limits on audit scope for £178.5m pension liability and property valuations, preventing verification
findings.detail: Management chose not to provide audit evidence for Property, Plant & Equipment, pensions, and grant income, classifying this as management-imposed limitation of scope. The pension liability of £178.5 million (31 March 2024) cannot be verified as management has not reconciled membership data and financial statements do not present a materially correct position. Property valuation issues from 2023/24 remain unresolved.
findings.matters: Management-imposed limitations mean material balances are unverified. A £178.5m pension liability and unresolved property valuations (typically material assets) mean readers cannot rely on core balance sheet figures. This raises questions about financial resilience and accuracy of reported net worth.
findings.figures: Pension fund deficit: £178.5m (31 March 2024); management-imposed scope limitations on PPE, pensions, and grant income
findings.quote: As evidence for these areas was either unavailable or could not be adequately supported, this constitutes a management-imposed limitation of scope.

findings.headline: Auditors will disclaim opinion on 2024/25 financial statements, continuing a pattern of four consecutive years with disclaimers
findings.detail: The council will receive a disclaimed audit opinion on the 2024/25 statements, following disclaimers for 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23, and 2023/24. Despite some improvements, auditors were unable to complete all planned procedures, particularly around PPE, pensions and grant income. Combined with unresolved comparatives and opening balances, auditors cannot conclude the statements are free from material misstatement.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means financial statements cannot be relied upon by lenders, investors or the council's own decision-makers. Four consecutive years of disclaimers indicates systematic issues beyond one-year anomalies, raising questions about the council's capacity to produce auditable accounts.
findings.figures: Cumulative disclaimed opinions: 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24, 2024/25 (five years); backstop date: 27 February 2026
findings.quote: we have been unable to complete all planned audit procedures. When combined with the lack of assurance over the comparatives and opening balances, we are unable to conclude that the 2024/25 financial statements are free from material and pervasive misstatement. We therefore anticipate issuing a disclaimed 2024/25 audit opinion.

findings.headline: Emerging concerns regarding procurement and contract management with systemic failures identified in a multi-party homecare contract
findings.detail: The council disclosed (transparently, in accordance with CIPFA guidance) systemic failures and irregularities in a multi-party homecare contract that operated from 2017 onwards. Issues included supplier oversight failures, supply chain management problems, payment irregularities and procurement process weaknesses. A detailed investigation was ongoing at the time of this statement. Broader procurement and contract management improvements are being implemented including quarterly financial review of key suppliers, monthly contract value monitoring, and new Power BI reporting tools.
findings.matters: Systemic failures in a major contract over eight years represent material control failures. The investigation is ongoing and could result in clawback, reputational damage, or further findings. This is also a trigger for the external auditor's statutory recommendation on procurement.
findings.figures: Homecare contract in operation from 2017 onwards; external investigations ongoing; investigation outcomes to be reported to public meetings
findings.quote: During 2023/24, several issues came to light concerning a multi-party Homecare contract that had been in operation from 2017 onwards. These concerned systemic failures and irregularities in relation to supplier oversight, supply chain management, payments to suppliers and procurement processes.

findings.headline: Adult Social Care facing financial sustainability issues; high-cost care package overspends being placed under director-level approval
findings.detail: Adult Social Care budget faces sustainability pressures requiring mitigations. Since April 2025, the Director is now approving any high-cost care packages and all new high-cost packages over £1k per week must be reviewed by a director to prevent cost drift. Adult Social Care budgets for 2025/26 have been realigned, though this suggests prior misalignment. Integration of finance and performance reporting is ongoing but has been slow to achieve.
findings.matters: Adult Social Care is a demand-led statutory service where cost pressures are hard to control. Director-level approval for packages over £1k per week suggests overspends have been a management issue. The need to realign 2025/26 budgets after the year has begun indicates forecasting weakness.
findings.figures: Director approval now required for high-cost packages over £1k per week (from April 2025); Adult Social Care budgets realigned for 2025/26
findings.quote: Since April 2025, the Director is now overseeing any high-cost packages and arranging any necessary reviews, any new high-cost packages (over £1k per week) must be approved and reviewed by a director to prevent drift in care overspend.

findings.headline: Children's Services facing significant SEND budget pressures with High Needs Block deficit and rising transport costs
findings.detail: The General Fund faces significant pressures from Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) provision, specifically from a high number of children being assessed for Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) which require more caseworkers and educational psychology time. SEN transport costs have risen significantly. A Transport Transformation Group has been established with proposals to save £2.2m over three years. An external funding review of SEND provision banding is underway. The statutory override for High Needs Block deficits has been extended to 2028 but remains a material pressure.
findings.matters: SEND pressures are rising across England but Tower Hamlets is identifying this as a significant governance issue requiring active mitigation. If transport savings (£2.2m over 3 years) are not delivered, this becomes a material structural deficit. This is a demand-led pressure that cannot easily be managed down.
findings.figures: Proposals to save c£2.2m over next 3 years from SEN transport review; High Needs Block deficit statutory override extended to 2028
findings.quote: Children's Services face significant pressures to the SEND General Fund due to the high number of children being assessed for an EHCP, which requires more caseworkers and educational psychology time. Additionally, SEN transport costs have risen.

findings.headline: Regulator of Social Housing issued C3 judgment for housing management in April 2025
findings.detail: Following a self-referral to the Regulator of Social Housing (RSH) in October 2024, the council's housing management service was inspected from November 2024 to March 2025 and received a C3 judgment (April 2025). This is described as 'shared with other London boroughs with similar density and ages of social housing stock' but indicates areas of non-compliance with Consumer Standards. The council is now in monthly Registered Provider Improvement meetings with RSH to track compliance.
findings.matters: A C3 judgment from the housing regulator indicates material compliance issues in a major council service. The council is required to demonstrate improvement to the regulator; failure to do so could result in escalated intervention. This is particularly significant given the council also brought Tower Hamlets Homes back in-house from 1 November 2023.
findings.figures: RSH judgment: C3 (April 2025); inspection period November 2024 to March 2025; monthly improvement meetings now in place
findings.quote: Subsequently the service was inspected by the RSH against the Consumer Standards, and we were given a C3 Judgement in April 2025.

findings.headline: Three statutory recommendations from external auditor EY covering accounts preparation, internal controls, and procurement
findings.detail: EY issued three formal statutory recommendations in its 2023/24 audit report under Section 24, Schedule 7 of the Local Audit and Accountability Act 2014. These cover: (1) reassessing roles and resources for financial reporting; ensuring audit evidence retention; and implementing corrective action plans. (2) Addressing internal control weaknesses and embedding a culture of continuous improvement. (3) Reviewing procurement arrangements and improving payment controls including segregation of duties and conflict of interest identification. All have been accepted with action plans approved by Audit Committee (March-April 2025).
findings.matters: Statutory recommendations are formal findings that the external auditor believes create material control weaknesses. They are publicly reported and tracked. Failure to implement them would typically result in a qualified audit opinion or escalation.
findings.figures: Three statutory recommendations; accepted by Audit Committee on 13 March 2025 (accounts and internal controls) and 24 April 2025 (procurement)
findings.quote: At the conclusion of the Council's 2023/24 audit, the Council's external auditor issued three statutory recommendations under Section 24, Schedule 7 of the Local Audit and Accountability Act 2014. These relate to Closing of the Annual Accounts, Internal Control and Procurement & Contract Management.

findings.headline: Homelessness costs in Tower Hamlets remain 'high and above budgeted provision' while London councils collectively overspent by £330m
findings.detail: The council faces a significant financial pressure from homelessness and temporary accommodation costs that are above budget. While demand and rent inflation are noted as partly external factors, the council's costs have not been contained within plan. London Councils described homelessness as 'the single biggest risk to its members' finances'. The council is implementing mitigations including procuring 500 private rented properties, purchasing 100 buyback properties, and using 100 HRA properties as temporary accommodation.
findings.matters: Homelessness is a statutory duty that cannot be avoided; if costs cannot be contained within the MTFS even with active mitigations, it represents a structural budget gap. This is the largest local government spending pressure across London.
findings.figures: London authorities collectively overspent by £330m on homelessness in 2024/25; Tower Hamlets costs remain 'high and above budgeted provision'
findings.quote: Collectively, Local Authorities in London overspent by £330m on homelessness in 2024/25. London Councils has described the homelessness crisis as the single biggest risk to its members' finances. In Tower Hamlets, the costs of meeting statutory homelessness duty and temporary accommodation remain high and above budgeted provision.

findings.headline: External audit issued disclaimer opinions for three consecutive years (2020/21-2022/23) and again for 2023/24
findings.detail: Deloitte issued disclaimer audit opinions (December 2024) on the council's 2020/21, 2021/22 and 2022/23 financial statements due to insufficient time to complete necessary audit work, plus other matters including failure to prepare group accounts, pension scheme entries, and officer remuneration disclosure errors. Ernst & Young (EY) subsequently issued a disclaimer opinion on the 2023/24 Statement of Accounts (February 2025) under backstop arrangements.
findings.matters: Multiple years of disclaimers indicate systematic weaknesses in financial reporting, record-keeping or audit trail that prevent external auditors from forming an opinion. This is material to credit assessment.
findings.figures: Deloitte audit completed December 2024; EY audit completed February 2025; EY also issued three statutory recommendations
findings.quote: These accounts were issued with disclaimer audit opinions by the external auditor owing to insufficient time being available complete the necessary audit work to form an audit opinion by the backstop date, and other reported matters including the failure to prepare group accounts, entries related to the pension scheme, and errors in the disclosure of officer remuneration.

findings.headline: Ministerial Directions imposed after Best Value Inspection found council failing Best Value Duty
findings.detail: On 22 January 2025, the Secretary of State issued Ministerial Directions establishing a statutory support package with Ministerial Envoys after finding the council was failing its Best Value Duty. The Directions cover governance, partnerships, community engagement, culture, leadership and continuous improvement, and remain in place until at least March 2028. The council retains executive decision-making powers but is subject to mentoring and oversight by three appointed Ministerial Envoys.
findings.matters: Government intervention of this scale signals fundamental governance weaknesses; lenders need to understand the nature of the failure and whether the improvement programme will be delivered.
findings.figures: Ministerial Directions issued 22 January 2025; inspection period 22 February 2024 to July 2024; report published 12 November 2024
findings.quote: The Ministerial Directions are clear that the Secretary of State at the time was satisfied that the Authority was failing to comply with its Best Value Duty, for the themes of Continuous Improvement, Governance, Leadership, Culture and Partnerships

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Report External Audit Dec 25
findings.headline: Accounts were historically qualified or disclaimed back to 2018/19, only recently resolved
findings.detail: The council has only recently resolved historic annual governance statements and accounts dating back to 2018/19 that were either qualified (2018-2020) or disclaimed (2020-2023). This means financial statements for a five-year period were not fully auditable, indicating long-term weaknesses in financial reporting that have only now been addressed.
findings.matters: Qualified and disclaimed accounts mean auditors could not give assurance over the financial position. This extends over multiple years and reflects systemic problems in financial reporting capability.
findings.figures: Accounts qualified 2018-2020; accounts disclaimed 2020-2023; only recently resolved
findings.quote: Financial resilience has improved through the publication of a Medium-Term Financial Strategy and the resolution of historic annual governance statements (AGS) and accounts dating back to 2018/19 which were qualified (2018-2020) and disclaimed (2020-23).

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Report External Audit Dec 25
findings.headline: Operation NextWage investigation involves potentially serious criminal offences including possible money laundering
findings.detail: One of two high-profile investigations informing EY's new statutory recommendation on investigations. Operation NextWage has not been formally reported to audit committee due to its sensitive and potentially criminal nature. The investigation was led internally by an experienced manager who has since left the council. The council has now commissioned specialist forensic e-discovery support for targeted email review to investigate if there has been additional wrongdoing beyond what internal investigation has uncovered.
findings.matters: A potential fraud or corruption matter involving possible money laundering is a serious governance, reputational, and legal risk to the council. The fact that the lead investigator has departed and an external forensic investigation has been commissioned suggests complexity and seriousness.
findings.figures: One high-profile investigation; forensic e-discovery support commissioned; council notes work is progressing and due to conclude by December 2025
findings.quote: The decision was taken, due to the sensitive and potentially criminal nature of the case, which may involve serious offences such as money laundering.

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Report External Audit Dec 25
findings.headline: Procurement waiver (RCDA) process had major control failures: no central register, no monitoring, and retrospective waivers issued
findings.detail: A comprehensive internal audit of the procurement waiver process (Record of Corporate Director Action) concluded in Nov 2024 and identified significant weaknesses: no central database of approved waivers, lack of monitoring and oversight, and absence of evidence of contracts between council and awarded providers. Internal audit made 6 high-risk recommendations; as of June 2025, 4 were not implemented and 2 partially implemented.
findings.matters: Procurement waivers bypass standard competitive tendering. Without central tracking, monitoring, or documented contracts, the council has weak controls over how contracts are awarded and managed, creating financial control and value-for-money risks.
findings.figures: 6 high-risk internal audit recommendations; 4 not implemented as of June 2025, 2 partially implemented; RFQ system now requires procurement approval for transactions over £5,000
findings.quote: The lack of a central database or register of approved procurement waivers; An overall lack of monitoring and oversight over procurement waivers

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Report External Audit Dec 25
findings.headline: Implementation rate of internal audit recommendations remains weak at 70% for 2024/25 (down from 82% for 2023/24)
findings.detail: The council has improved implementation tracking since Feb 2025, but the implementation rate for recommendations from internal audit's Limited Assurance reports stands at 70% for 2024/25, indicating that three in ten audit-flagged control weaknesses are not being acted on. This was 82% for 2023/24.
findings.matters: A high rate of unimplemented audit recommendations indicates weaknesses in the control environment are persisting rather than being fixed, raising questions about the council's ability to address known risks.
findings.figures: 70% implementation rate 2024/25; 82% for 2023/24; previously reported as 56% for 2024/25 by EY at time of interim report (later revised up to 70%)
findings.quote: Subsequently, the current position is an implementation rate of 82% in relation to 2023/24 and 70% for 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Report External Audit Dec 25
findings.headline: Accounts audit still has 16 incomplete workstreams and only partial assurance on one account area, affecting reliability of financial statements
findings.detail: The 2024/25 audit shows improvement from 2023/24 (24 workstreams completed vs 15 previously, 6 account areas with substantial assurance vs 4), but 16 workstreams remain incomplete. The council had to re-present debtors and creditors disclosures, rebuild HRA working papers, and address income tracing issues. Final assurance results remain subject to further review by EY partners.
findings.matters: Incomplete audit workstreams and partial assurance mean the financial statements have not received full external audit clearance, which directly undermines the reliability of reported financial position.
findings.figures: 6 account areas with substantial assurance, 1 with partial assurance (2024/25); 16 workstreams incomplete; 24 workstreams completed vs 15 in prior year
findings.quote: A total of 16 workstreams were not completed, largely due to the prioritisation of key areas of work, which primarily focused on prioritising balance sheet items.

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Report External Audit Dec 25
findings.headline: Section 151 Officer remains on acting-up basis; permanent recruitment has been unsuccessful and remains ongoing as of September 2025
findings.detail: The permanent S151 Officer position has not been filled. A recruitment consultant was engaged; the post was most recently advertised in early September 2025, with the consultant noting that demand for S151 talent is at an all-time high and that Tower Hamlets' scale and challenges make recruitment particularly difficult. EY specifically recommended urgent steps to appoint a permanent S151.
findings.matters: The Section 151 Officer is the council's chief financial officer and key governance officer. An acting arrangement in a council under audit stress, with multiple governance failures identified, creates continuity risk and raises questions about financial leadership stability.
findings.figures: Acting-up arrangement in place; post most recently advertised early September 2025; ongoing recruitment
findings.quote: The consultants advised that recruiting to these roles was proving significantly challenging as demand for S151 talent is at an all-time high and the councils search for an experienced S151 was making the search even harder because of the scale of the role and challenge.

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Report External Audit Dec 25
findings.headline: External auditor issued four new statutory recommendations and six significant weaknesses in Feb-Nov 2025, indicating persistent governance failures
findings.detail: In February 2025, EY issued three statutory recommendations on accounts closing, internal controls, and procurement. In the 2024/25 interim VfM report issued November 2025, EY identified six additional significant weaknesses including internal audit effectiveness, annual governance statement quality, audit committee effectiveness, housing, investigations processes, and the Golden Triangle (senior leadership stability).
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether the council's financial reporting, controls, and governance structures are reliable enough to manage public funds and whether the audit findings suggest deeper operational problems.
findings.figures: Three statutory recommendations (Feb 2025); six additional significant weaknesses identified (Nov 2025); these follow similar findings from Deloitte covering 2018/19 to 2022/23
findings.quote: the 2024/25 Interim VfM Report has identified six additional significant weaknesses, being: Effectiveness of the Internal Audit Function, Annual Governance Statement, factors impacting The Golden Triangle, Audit Committee effectiveness, Housing and an additional draft statutory recommendation relating to the effectiveness of the council's process for conducting internal investigations

news_drafts.headline: £27m pension contribution reduction has been achieved through the triennial valuation.
news_drafts.lead: While it helps 2026-27, this saving is not sustainable year-on-year. If the council's other savings underperform, it cannot rely on this contribution again to fill the gap.

news_drafts.headline: Transformation and technology savings totalling £6m+ are either at risk or marked unlikely.
news_drafts.lead: If transformation programmes are not delivering, it suggests capability or planning issues within the council, raising questions about whether other complex change initiatives can be trusted.

news_drafts.headline: Income generation proposals representing approximately £4.8m are at risk or unlikely.
news_drafts.lead: Income-dependent savings are more fragile than cost-cutting and harder for a council to guarantee. Heavy reliance on income that isn't materialising increases budget risk.
